test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a correct use of baking soda (sodium hydrogen carbonate) in daily life?

options.text: It is used to make soaps non-greasy
It is used to neutralise strong acids in lead-acid batteries
It is used to prepare edible salts
It is used in fire extinguishers to produce foam

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is used in fire extinguishers to produce foam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium hydrogen carbonate (baking soda)** is a crucial component in certain fire extinguishers. It reacts with acid to release **carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas**, which helps in extinguishing fire by displacing oxygen and creating a foam.
 
• This foam acts as a barrier to prevent the fire from spreading further and helps in cooling the burning material.
 
• When baking soda is used in fire extinguishers, it decomposes upon heating to release carbon dioxide and water vapor, which are effective in putting out flames.
 
• The reaction can be represented as:

 **2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂**.
 
• These extinguishers are particularly effective in dealing with **Class B and Class C fires**, which involve flammable liquids and gases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uses of Baking Soda:**

 
 
• **Option 1**: It is used to make soaps non-greasy. This is **incorrect** because baking soda is not commonly used in soap manufacturing to remove grease.
 
• **Option 2**: It is used to neutralize strong acids in lead-acid batteries. This is **incorrect** because, while baking soda can neutralize acids, it is not specifically used for lead-acid batteries.
 
• **Option 3**: It is used to prepare edible salts. This is **incorrect** because baking soda itself is an edible salt but is not primarily used to prepare other salts.
 
• **Option 4**: It is used in fire extinguishers to produce foam. This is **correct** because baking soda reacts to release carbon dioxide, forming foam to extinguish fires.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Baking Soda:**
 
 
• Its chemical formula is **NaHCO₃**, and it is a mild alkali.
 
• It is commonly used as a leavening agent in baking due to the release of carbon dioxide gas during decomposition.
 
• Baking soda is also used as a cleaning agent, deodorizer, and in medical applications for neutralizing stomach acid.
 
 
 
• **Types of Fire Extinguishers:**
 
 
• Fire extinguishers are categorized based on the types of fires they are designed to combat, such as Class A, B, C, D, and electrical fires.
 
• Baking soda-based extinguishers are effective against Class B (flammable liquids) and Class C (electrical) fires.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The use of baking soda in fire extinguishers is environmentally friendly because it produces non-toxic byproducts like sodium carbonate, water, and carbon dioxide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction in Fire Extinguishers:** Baking soda reacts with acids like sulfuric acid to produce carbon dioxide, which extinguishes fire.
 
• **Handling Fires:** Always use the appropriate type of fire extinguisher depending on the material involved in the fire (e.g., wood, liquid, gas, or electrical equipment).
 
• **Storage and Safety:** Baking soda-based fire extinguishers should be stored in accessible locations and inspected regularly for proper functionality.
